messages:
carmen: heads-up: planning a preemptive maintenance window for scheduler nodes in eu-central due to a BMC/network firmware push from the colo team. targeting next Tue 02:00-04:00 UTC.
liam: is this just control-plane nodes or whole racks?
carmen: only scheduler/control-plane VMs + their BMCs. not touching worker GPU hosts, but we'll need to cordon and gracefully evacuate pods that rely on scheduler affinity rules.
priya: ok — what's the evacuation plan? we should avoid expensive backfills during business hours for Dedicated pools.
carmen: plan A: stagger by cohort (4 cohorts), 15min drain + 30min watch per cohort. use canary cohort to validate autoscaler and backfill behavior.
andre: suggest adding a temporary scaling policy: allow burst-up to +10% capacity for 20m per cohort to avoid throttling on critical long-running inferences. noted Dedicated customers must be informed.
liam: how do we implement the drains? putting the command here for reference:
```
# cordon then drain keeping daemonsets, delete local data
kubectl cordon redwood-scheduler-1
kubectl drain redwood-scheduler-1 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=120
```
priya: add `--force` only if node is stuck. also add a preflight check to ensure KV-cache warmers are primed in fallback pool.
infra-bot: Reminder: maintenance window created in ops-calendar: https://calendar.redwood.internal/m/3071122334
andre: can we route new requests to eu-west for the window? latency will degrade but better than errors. need routing policy change for 2h.
carmen: routing change approved for canary + low-tier workloads. we'll keep high-tier pinned and notify customers with SLA. ops-oncall can you take the customer comms draft?
ops-oncall: on it. i'll ping sales + success to review wording. draft will mention expected short queueing for ephemeral jobs and fallback to eu-west.
liam: cost note: extra backfill capacity will add ~0.6% hourly GPU usage for that day. estimate multiregion egress bump ~12GB/hr.
priya: I'll run a quick sim on the queuing model today and post results. if it looks bad we tighten cohort windows.
andre: one more: BMC firmware has a small chance (~0.3%) to hit a hung microcontroller requiring rack-level power cycle -> fallback plan to move affected racks to cooldown cohort and extend watch to 90m.
carmen: agreed. final steps: update runbook, create pager for any schedule slippage, and run a preflight at T-24h. thanks all :thumbsup:
ops-oncall: done — runbook link: https://runbooks.redwood.internal/maintenance/preemptive-scheduler-evac-3071122334
priya: posted queuing sim: peak queue delay predicted +120ms for non-pinned routes. will re-evaluate after canary.
liam: canary start set to 02:00 UTC cohort A. I'll be on call.
andre: I'll monitor autoscaler and patch BGP egress rules if needed.
infra-bot: scheduled: maintenance started by carmen at 02:00 UTC.
